note: Bytes in and bytes out (CyberChef's Input and Output encodings are chain steps such as hex:decode and hex:encode). The key and the IV are key params in any of the key encodings, the key 16, 24 or 32 bytes. The mode is CBC (the default), CFB, OFB, CTR, GCM or ECB, and padding is its own choice (pkcs7, the default, or none), where CyberChef has separate CBC/NoPadding and ECB/NoPadding modes. GCM takes the additional data as the aad param and appends the 16-byte tag to the ciphertext, where CyberChef returns the tag separately. A wrong key or IV length is E_RANGE. CTR adds one to the last four bytes of the counter block only, modulo 2^32 with no carry into the rest, as CyberChef does (node-forge's inc32); a whole-block counter (the usual reading of SP 800-38A) gives the same key stream until the low word wraps, after 2^32 blocks. GCM needs an IV of at least 8 bytes (E_RANGE otherwise; CyberChef accepts any length, even none, which the library behind Forge does not). An empty IV is E_RANGE in CBC, CFB, OFB and CTR as in CyberChef. CyberChef's Include IV in output (Off, Prepend, Append) is a chain step: cat the IV in front of or behind the output.

The inverse of aes:encrypt with the same parameters. For GCM the last 16 bytes of the input are the tag (CyberChef takes a separate GCM Tag param), and a tag that does not verify is E_COERCE and returns no plaintext; bad PKCS#7 padding is E_COERCE too. The no-padding modes of CyberChef are padding none. CyberChef's IV from input (From start or From end) is a chain step: slice the IV off the input and pass it as the iv param. CTR counts as in aes:encrypt (the last four bytes).
